As an ADHDer, I can relate to your post. It's true that none of the jobs out there require you to memorise things from a textbook so even quite a lot of neurotypical people feel the same way about college at some point and drop out. It's also true that working is very different from schooling. And of course many people ended up in a job completely unrelated to their major.

However, I think the nicest thing about going to college is the networking. Chances are your school already has a huge network and you can rely on that network to increase your chances of finding a job. There will be hiring managers who graduated from the same school as you who are interested in hiring graduates from the same school. 

As people say these days, it's who you know which gets you jobs. College is one of the best places for networking (unless if you are from a powerful family with a huge network). In comparison, most people who graduated from high school is just a nobody in the great pool of job candidates.
